checks.check: All six declared os/arch policy identities retain Node22.22.1/npm10.9.4/header22.22.1 consistency; profile metadata is derived from verified official archive/assets and reproducible, not copied from an installed receipt.
checks.evidence: runtime-policy.json is unchanged. The generator verifies pinned asset sizes and SHA256, checks npm/header versions, and derives inventory metadata in memory. The daemon-passed reproduction test compares all six derived profiles with the pinned profiles.

checks.check: Completion64KiB, inventory16MiB,32768 entries,128MiB/file,1GiB expanded,256MiB/compressed asset,600s network and120s verification bounds are explicit and tested.
checks.evidence: RUNTIME_LIMITS explicitly declares every listed bound. runtime-policy.test.ts asserts the exact complete object; production-deadlines.test.ts checks actual timeout arguments. Both passed according to the daemon.

checks.check: RuntimeIdentity/ReleaseManifest/IPC fields remain unchanged; metadata computation alone neither executes target code nor enables a native target.
checks.evidence: The implementation leaves contracts, schemas and daemon IPC unchanged. The reproduction test forbids subprocess execution and filesystem extraction/allocation during derivation. Native qualification remains a separate publisher check.

checks.check: Keep original archive/profile/inventory/completion bytes, hashes and public fields unchanged; POSIX mode protection is a verifier/publication rule, not regenerated official content or a new runtime identity/layout.
checks.evidence: Pinned policy, inventory/completion serializers and runtime layout are unchanged. runtime-metadata.ts adds only the internal RuntimeProtection union alongside the deadline import change; it does not rewrite modes or official metadata.

checks.check: Ordinary production entrypoint import and runtime/download deadline behavior are unchanged for unset, normal, slow-vm and invalid INSRC_QUALIFICATION_PROFILE; remove indirect production import-time selector failure as well as direct runtime-metadata/download coupling.
checks.evidence: Production consumers and transitive harness context now import environment-independent operation-time-budgets.mjs. The daemon-passed production test covers unset, normal, slow-vm, invalid and empty selectors, importing manager/terminal and exercising resolver, coordinator, Git and download deadline paths.

checks.check: Only explicit trusted qualification invocation installs bounded process-local context before relevant modules load; preserve approved normal/slow-VM harness propagation without exposing a wire/receipt/ambient-env override or changing unrelated completed harness contracts.
checks.evidence: The explicit qualification preloader admits a frozen normal/slow-vm policy into process-local context; ordinary policy imports do not read the selector. Trusted child launches propagate the preloader. Tests retain exact role budgets, immutable snapshots, conflict rejection and explicit short overrides; wire and receipt contracts are unchanged.

checks.check: Exercise normal manager/terminal/resolver import and relevant action paths with every selector case, including transitive budget imports; qualification-only invalid selectors retain their typed diagnostic. Actual native execution/publication eligibility is release-owned and separate from six-target profile metadata; deferred Windows and unqualified arch/baseline combinations cannot self-enable.
checks.evidence: The required test bodies exercise the advertised imports/actions and timeout values. Invalid qualification selectors assert qualification-profile-invalid before I/O or worker admission. Six-target tests require qualification rejection without evidence; packaging retains exact target/baseline/runtime/addon qualification checks independently of profile metadata.

verdict.reason: All acceptance checks are supported by repository code and meaningful daemon-passed tests; implementation changes stay within deadline isolation, trusted qualification propagation, internal lane typing and supporting fixtures/assets.
